title: 1. Bono de Empleados (Employee Bonus)
description:
Escribe una consulta SQL para reportar el nombre de cada empleado y el monto de su bono para todos los empleados que tengan un bono **menor a 1000** o **que no tengan ningún bono** (valor `NULL`).

### Tabla: `Employee`
| Column Name | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| empId | int |
| name | varchar |
| supervisor | int |
| salary | int |

### Tabla: `Bonus`
| Column Name | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| empId | int |
| bonus | int |

### Formato de Salida
| name | bonus |
| :--- | :--- |
| Brad | null |
| John | null |
| Dan | 500 |
seedDML:

INSERT INTO Bonus VALUES (2, 500), (4, 2000), (5, 1000);
starterCode:
SELECT 
FROM Employee e
LEFT JOIN Bonus b ON e.empId = b.empId
WHERE ...;
solutionSQL:
SELECT e.name, b.bonus
FROM Employee e
LEFT JOIN Bonus b ON e.empId = b.empId
WHERE b.bonus < 1000 OR b.bonus IS NULL;

title: 4. Tiempo Promedio por Máquina (ROUND)
description:
Hay una tabla con logs de máquinas de fábrica. Cada proceso tiene un evento `start` y un evento `end`.
Calcula el tiempo promedio que le toma a cada máquina completar un proceso.
El tiempo debe redondearse a **3 decimales** con el nombre `processing_time`.

### Tabla: `Activity`
| machine_id | process_id | activity_type | timestamp |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | 0 | start | 0.712 |
| 0 | 0 | end | 1.520 |
| 0 | 1 | start | 3.140 |
| 0 | 1 | end | 4.120 |
| 1 | 0 | start | 0.550 |
| 1 | 0 | end | 1.550 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Activity;
CREATE TABLE Activity (machine_id INT, process_id INT, activity_type VARCHAR(10), timestamp FLOAT);
solutionSQL:
SELECT 
    a1.machine_id,
    ROUND(AVG(a2.timestamp - a1.timestamp), 3) AS processing_time
FROM Activity a1
JOIN Activity a2 
  ON a1.machine_id = a2.machine_id 
 AND a1.process_id = a2.process_id 
 AND a1.activity_type = 'start' 
 AND a2.activity_type = 'end'
GROUP BY a1.machine_id;

title: 5. Tasa de Confirmación (Confirmation Rate)
description:
La tasa de confirmación de un usuario es el número de mensajes `confirmed` dividido por el número total de solicitudes enviadas.
Si un usuario no envió ninguna solicitud, su tasa de confirmación debe ser `0.00`.
Redondea el resultado a **2 decimales** con el alias `confirmation_rate`.

### Tabla: `Signups`
| user_id |
| :--- |
| 3 |
| 7 |
| 2 |

### Tabla: `Confirmations`
| user_id | action |
| :--- | :--- |
| 3 | timeout |
| 3 | confirmed |
| 7 | confirmed |
| 7 | confirmed |
seedDML:
INSERT INTO Signups VALUES (3), (7), (2);
INSERT INTO Confirmations VALUES (3, 'timeout'), (3, 'confirmed'), (7, 'confirmed'), (7, 'confirmed');
starterCode:
SELECT s.user_id, ... AS confirmation_rate
FROM Signups s
LEFT JOIN Confirmations c ON s.user_id = c.user_id
GROUP BY s.user_id;
solutionSQL:
SELECT 
    s.user_id,
    ROUND(IFNULL(AVG(c.action = 'confirmed'), 0), 2) AS confirmation_rate
FROM Signups s
LEFT JOIN Confirmations c ON s.user_id = c.user_id
GROUP BY s.user_id;

title: 6. Visitas sin Transacción (Anti-Join con ON AND)
description:
Encuentra los IDs de los usuarios que visitaron el centro comercial pero no realizaron ninguna transacción, y el conteo de cuántas veces ocurrió esto.
Nombra las columnas `customer_id` y `count_no_trans`.

| visit_id | customer_id |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 23 |
| 2 | 9 |
| 4 | 30 |
| 5 | 54 |

### Tabla: `Transactions`
| transaction_id | visit_id | amount |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | 5 | 310 |
| 3 | 5 | 300 |
seedDML:
INSERT INTO Visits VALUES (1, 23), (2, 9), (4, 30), (5, 54);
INSERT INTO Transactions VALUES (2, 5, 310), (3, 5, 300);
solutionSQL:

title: 7. Triple Join: Clientes, Pedidos y Catálogo
description:
Calcula el gasto total realizado por cada cliente sumando `quantity * price`.
Incluye a todos los clientes registrados, incluso si no han realizado compras (en cuyo caso su gasto total debe ser `0`).
Nombra las columnas `customer_name` y `total_spent`. Ordena por `total_spent` descendente.

### Tabla: `Customers`
| Column Name | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| id | int |
| name | varchar |

### Tabla: `Products`
| Column Name | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| id | int |
| name | varchar |
| price | decimal |

### Tabla: `Orders`
| Column Name | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| id | int |
| customer_id | int |
| product_id | int |
| quantity | int |

### Formato de Salida
| customer_name | total_spent |
| :--- | :--- |
| Alice | 1050.00 |
| Bob | 25.00 |
| Charlie | 0.00 |
starterCode:
SELECT c.name AS customer_name, ...
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON ...
LEFT JOIN Products p ON ...
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
solutionSQL:
SELECT 
    c.name AS customer_name,
    IFNULL(SUM(o.quantity * p.price), 0) AS total_spent
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN Products p ON o.product_id = p.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

title: 8. Self-Join: Empleados y sus Supervisores
description:

| age | int |

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

schemaDDL:

CREATE TABLE Employees (employee_id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(50), reports_to INT, age INT);

(6, 'Alice', 9, 41),
(4, 'Bob', 9, 36),

starterCode:

FROM Employees emp
JOIN Employees mgr ON ...

    mgr.name,
    COUNT(emp.employee_id) AS reports_count,
    ROUND(AVG(emp.age)) AS average_age
FROM Employees emp

| 1 | 1 | 2019-07-20 | open_session |

| 2 | 4 | 2019-07-20 | open_session |
| 2 | 4 | 2019-07-21 | open_session |
| 3 | 2 | 2019-06-25 | open_session |

title: 11. Deduplicación Analítica con ROW_NUMBER()
description:

### Tabla: `Person`

| id | int |
| email | varchar |
| name | varchar |

### Formato de Salida
| id | email | name |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | john@example.com | John Doe |
| 2 | bob@example.com | Bob Ross |
| 4 | alice@example.com | Alice Smith |
schemaDDL:

CREATE TABLE Person (id INT PRIMARY KEY, email VARCHAR(100), name VARCHAR(50));
seedDML:
INSERT INTO Person VALUES

(2, 'bob@example.com', 'Bob Ross'),
(3, 'john@example.com', 'John Aaron'),
(4, 'alice@example.com', 'Alice Smith');
starterCode:

    SELECT id, email, name, ... AS rn
    FROM Person
)

FROM RankedPersons

        id, 
        email, 
        name,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY id ASC) AS rn
    FROM Person

FROM RankedPersons
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY id;

title: 16. Chained CTEs: Región Líder en Ventas
description:
Tienes las ventas por sucursal y la región a la que pertenece cada una.
Usa **dos CTEs encadenadas**:
1. `RegionalSales`: Calcula la venta total por región.
2. `TopRegion`: Selecciona la región con la venta total máxima.
En la consulta final, reporta los nombres de las sucursales y sus ventas individuales que pertenezcan a dicha región líder.
Columnas: `branch_name`, `sales`. Ordena por `sales` desc.

### Tabla: `Branches`
| Column Name | Type |
| :--- | :--- |
| id | int |
| branch_name | varchar |
| region | varchar |
| sales | decimal |

### Formato de Salida
| branch_name | sales |
| :--- | :--- |
| Soyapango Plaza | 22000.00 |
| San Salvador Central | 15000.00 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Branches;
CREATE TABLE Branches (id INT PRIMARY KEY, branch_name VARCHAR(50), region VARCHAR(20), sales DECIMAL(10,2));
seedDML:
INSERT INTO Branches VALUES 
(1, 'San Salvador Central', 'Central', 15000.00),
(2, 'Soyapango Plaza', 'Central', 22000.00),
(3, 'Santa Ana Centro', 'Occidente', 12000.00),
(4, 'Sonsonate Puerto', 'Occidente', 8000.00),
(5, 'San Miguel Triángulo', 'Oriente', 19000.00);
starterCode:
WITH RegionalSales AS (
    SELECT region, SUM(sales) AS total_sales
    FROM Branches
    GROUP BY region
),
TopRegion AS (
    SELECT region
    FROM RegionalSales
    ORDER BY total_sales DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT b.branch_name, b.sales
FROM Branches b
JOIN TopRegion tr ON b.region = tr.region
ORDER BY b.sales DESC;
solutionSQL:
WITH RegionalSales AS (
    SELECT region, SUM(sales) AS total_sales
    FROM Branches
    GROUP BY region
),
TopRegion AS (
    SELECT region
    FROM RegionalSales
    ORDER BY total_sales DESC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT b.branch_name, b.sales
FROM Branches b
JOIN TopRegion tr ON b.region = tr.region
ORDER BY b.sales DESC;

title: 19. Números Consecutivos (LEAD / LAG)
description:
Encuentra todos los números que aparecen al menos tres veces consecutivas en la tabla de logs.
Retorna el resultado en la columna `ConsecutiveNums` sin duplicados.

| :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 1 |
| 2 | 2 |
| 3 | 1 |
| 7 | 2 |
| 8 | 1 |
| 9 | 1 |
| 15 | 1 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Logs;
CREATE TABLE Logs (id INT PRIMARY KEY, num INT);
starterCode:
WITH RankedLogs AS (
    SELECT 
        num,
        LAG(num, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev_num,
        LEAD(num, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num
    FROM Logs
)
SELECT DISTINCT num AS ConsecutiveNums
FROM RankedLogs
WHERE ...;
solutionSQL:
WITH RankedLogs AS (
    SELECT 
        num,
        LAG(num, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS prev_num,
        LEAD(num, 1) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS next_num
    FROM Logs
)
SELECT DISTINCT num AS ConsecutiveNums
FROM RankedLogs
WHERE num = prev_num AND num = next_num;

schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS BankTransactions;
CREATE TABLE BankTransactions (id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT, transaction_date DATE, amount DECIMAL(10,2));
starterCode:
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    transaction_date,
    amount,
    SUM(amount) OVER (
        PARTITION BY ...
        ORDER BY ...
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS running_total
FROM BankTransactions

solutionSQL:

title: 22. Niveles del Organigrama (WITH RECURSIVE)
description:
Dada la tabla `Org`, reporta cada empleado con su nivel jerárquico (`level`). El CEO (sin manager) está en nivel 1; sus reportes directos en nivel 2, etc.
Columnas: `id`, `name`, `level`. Ordena por `level`, `id`.

### Tabla: `Org`
| id | name | manager_id |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Ana | NULL |
| 2 | Luis | 1 |
| 3 | Marta | 1 |
| 4 | Pedro | 2 |
| 5 | Sofía | 4 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Org;
CREATE TABLE Org (id INT PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(50), manager_id INT);
starterCode:
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
    SELECT id, name, 1 AS level
    FROM Org
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT ...
)
SELECT id, name, level FROM tree ORDER BY level, id;
solutionSQL:
WITH RECURSIVE tree AS (
    SELECT id, name, 1 AS level
    FROM Org
    WHERE manager_id IS NULL
    UNION ALL
    SELECT o.id, o.name, t.level + 1
    FROM Org o
    JOIN tree t ON o.manager_id = t.id
)
SELECT id, name, level FROM tree ORDER BY level, id;

title: 23. Calendario con Días sin Pedidos
description:
Reporta el número de pedidos por día para **todos** los días del 2023-01-01 al 2023-01-07, incluyendo los días sin pedidos (con `0`).
Columnas: `day`, `orders_count`. Ordena por `day`.
*Pista:* genera la serie de fechas con una CTE recursiva y haz `LEFT JOIN`.

### Tabla: `Orders`
| id | order_date |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 2023-01-01 |
| 2 | 2023-01-01 |
| 3 | 2023-01-03 |
| 4 | 2023-01-06 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Orders;
CREATE TABLE Orders (id INT PRIMARY KEY, order_date DATE);
starterCode:
WITH RECURSIVE days AS (
    SELECT DATE('2023-01-01') AS day
    UNION ALL
    SELECT ...
)
SELECT d.day, COUNT(o.id) AS orders_count
FROM days d
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON ...
GROUP BY d.day
ORDER BY d.day;
solutionSQL:
WITH RECURSIVE days AS (
    SELECT DATE('2023-01-01') AS day
    UNION ALL
    SELECT DATE_ADD(day, INTERVAL 1 DAY) FROM days WHERE day < '2023-01-07'
)
SELECT d.day, COUNT(o.id) AS orders_count
FROM days d
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON o.order_date = d.day
GROUP BY d.day
ORDER BY d.day;

title: 24. Ventas por Trimestre (Pivot)
description:
Convierte las ventas por trimestre en columnas. Una fila por producto con `q1`, `q2`, `q3`, `q4` (0 si no hubo ventas). Ordena por `product`.

### Tabla: `Sales`

| Laptop | Q2 | 150 |
| Mouse | Q1 | 20 |
| Mouse | Q4 | 35 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Sales;
CREATE TABLE Sales (product VARCHAR(30), quarter CHAR(2), amount INT);
starterCode:
SELECT product,
       SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q1' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q1
       -- q2, q3, q4 ...
FROM Sales
GROUP BY product
ORDER BY product;
solutionSQL:
SELECT product,
       SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q1' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q1,
       SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q2' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q2,
       SUM(CASE WHEN quarter = 'Q3' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS q3,

FROM Sales

title: 25. Occupations (HackerRank Classic)
description:
Pivota la tabla `Occupations` para que cada ocupación sea una columna (`Doctor`, `Professor`, `Singer`, `Actor`, en ese orden) con los nombres ordenados alfabéticamente. Si una columna se queda sin nombres, muestra `NULL`.

### Tabla: `Occupations`
| name | occupation |
| :--- | :--- |
| Samantha | Doctor |
| Julia | Actor |
| Maria | Actor |
| Meera | Singer |
| Ashely | Professor |
| Ketty | Professor |
| Christeen | Professor |
| Jane | Actor |
| Jenny | Doctor |
| Priya | Singer |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Occupations;
CREATE TABLE Occupations (name VARCHAR(30), occupation VARCHAR(30));
starterCode:
SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN occupation = 'Doctor' THEN name END) AS Doctor
    -- Professor, Singer, Actor ...
FROM (
    SELECT name, occupation,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY occupation ORDER BY name) AS rn
    FROM Occupations
) t
GROUP BY rn
ORDER BY rn;
solutionSQL:
SELECT
    MAX(CASE WHEN occupation = 'Doctor'    THEN name END) AS Doctor,
    MAX(CASE WHEN occupation = 'Professor' THEN name END) AS Professor,
    MAX(CASE WHEN occupation = 'Singer'    THEN name END) AS Singer,
    MAX(CASE WHEN occupation = 'Actor'     THEN name END) AS Actor
FROM (
    SELECT name, occupation,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY occupation ORDER BY name) AS rn
    FROM Occupations
) t
GROUP BY rn
ORDER BY rn;

title: 26. Media Móvil de 3 Días (ROWS BETWEEN)
description:
Para cada día calcula el promedio de ventas de ese día y los 2 anteriores (`moving_avg`, redondeado a 2 decimales). Los primeros días usan los registros disponibles.

| 2023-01-05 | 500 |
schemaDDL:

starterCode:

title: 28. Rachas de Login Consecutivas (Gaps & Islands)
description:
Encuentra, por usuario, cada racha de días consecutivos de login. Reporta `user_id`, `start_date`, `end_date`, `days`. Ordena por `user_id`, `start_date`.
*Pista:* `login_date - ROW_NUMBER()` es constante dentro de una racha.

### Tabla: `Logins`
| user_id | login_date |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 2023-01-01 |
| 1 | 2023-01-02 |
| 1 | 2023-01-03 |
| 1 | 2023-01-06 |
| 2 | 2023-01-02 |
| 2 | 2023-01-04 |
| 2 | 2023-01-05 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Logins;
CREATE TABLE Logins (user_id INT, login_date DATE, PRIMARY KEY (user_id, login_date));
starterCode:
WITH numbered AS (
    SELECT user_id, login_date,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS rn
    FROM Logins
),
grouped AS (
    SELECT user_id, login_date,
           DATE_SUB(login_date, INTERVAL rn DAY) AS grp
    FROM numbered
)
SELECT user_id, MIN(login_date) AS start_date, MAX(login_date) AS end_date, COUNT(*) AS days
FROM grouped
GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY user_id, start_date;
solutionSQL:
WITH numbered AS (
    SELECT user_id, login_date,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY login_date) AS rn
    FROM Logins
),
grouped AS (
    SELECT user_id, login_date,
           DATE_SUB(login_date, INTERVAL rn DAY) AS grp
    FROM numbered
)
SELECT user_id, MIN(login_date) AS start_date, MAX(login_date) AS end_date, COUNT(*) AS days
FROM grouped
GROUP BY user_id, grp
ORDER BY user_id, start_date;

title: 29. Retención de Día 1 (LeetCode 550)
description:
Reporta la fracción de jugadores que volvieron a iniciar sesión el **día siguiente a su primer login**, redondeada a 2 decimales, como `fraction`.

### Tabla: `Activity`
| player_id | event_date | games_played |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 2016-03-01 | 5 |
| 1 | 2016-03-02 | 6 |
| 2 | 2017-06-25 | 1 |
| 3 | 2016-03-02 | 0 |
| 3 | 2018-07-03 | 5 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Activity;
CREATE TABLE Activity (player_id INT, event_date DATE, games_played INT, PRIMARY KEY (player_id, event_date));
starterCode:
WITH first_login AS (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date) AS first_date
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
)
SELECT ROUND(... / ..., 2) AS fraction
FROM first_login f
JOIN Activity a ON ...;
solutionSQL:
WITH first_login AS (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date) AS first_date
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
)
SELECT ROUND(
    COUNT(DISTINCT a.player_id) / (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_id) FROM Activity), 2
) AS fraction
FROM first_login f
JOIN Activity a
  ON a.player_id = f.player_id
 AND a.event_date = DATE_ADD(f.first_date, INTERVAL 1 DAY);

title: 30. Reporte Mensual de Transacciones (LeetCode 1193)
description:
Por mes (`YYYY-MM`) y país reporta: `trans_count`, `approved_count`, `trans_total_amount`, `approved_total_amount`.
Columnas: `month`, `country`, `trans_count`, `approved_count`, `trans_total_amount`, `approved_total_amount`. Ordena por `month`, `country`.

### Tabla: `Transactions`
| id | country | state | amount | trans_date |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 121 | US | approved | 1000 | 2018-12-18 |
| 122 | US | declined | 2000 | 2018-12-19 |
| 123 | US | approved | 2000 | 2019-01-01 |
| 124 | DE | approved | 2000 | 2019-01-07 |
| 125 | CA | declined | 500 | 2019-01-15 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS Transactions;
CREATE TABLE Transactions (id INT PRIMARY KEY, country VARCHAR(10), state VARCHAR(10), amount INT, trans_date DATE);
starterCode:
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(trans_date, '%Y-%m') AS month,
       country,
       COUNT(*) AS trans_count
       -- approved_count, trans_total_amount, approved_total_amount
FROM Transactions
GROUP BY month, country
ORDER BY month, country;
solutionSQL:
SELECT DATE_FORMAT(trans_date, '%Y-%m') AS month,
       country,
       COUNT(*) AS trans_count,
       SUM(state = 'approved') AS approved_count,
       SUM(amount) AS trans_total_amount,
       SUM(CASE WHEN state = 'approved' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS approved_total_amount
FROM Transactions
GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(trans_date, '%Y-%m'), country
ORDER BY month, country;

Si hay empates en algún nivel de salario, repórtalos a todos (usando `DENSE_RANK() <= 3`).

starterCode:

solutionSQL:

description:

title: 34. Comparativa de Rankings: ROW_NUMBER vs RANK vs DENSE_RANK
description:
Para dominar y visualizar la diferencia matemática exacta entre las tres funciones de ranking de SQL, calcula las tres simultáneamente para cada estudiante según su calificación (`score`).
Retorna: `student_name`, `score`, `row_num`, `rank_num`, `dense_rank_num`.

- Para `row_num`: desempata alfabéticamente por `student_name ASC` (`ORDER BY score DESC, student_name ASC`).
- Para `rank_num`: ordena por `score DESC`.
- Para `dense_rank_num`: ordena por `score DESC`.

Ordena la consulta final por `score` DESC, `student_name` ASC.

### Tabla: `ExamScores`
| id | student_name | score |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | Alice | 100 |
| 2 | Bob | 100 |
| 3 | Charlie | 90 |
| 4 | David | 85 |
| 5 | Eva | 85 |
| 6 | Frank | 70 |
schemaDDL:
DROP TABLE IF EXISTS ExamScores;
CREATE TABLE ExamScores (id INT PRIMARY KEY, student_name VARCHAR(50), score INT);
starterCode:
SELECT 
    student_name,
    score,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) AS row_num,
    RANK() OVER (...) AS rank_num,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (...) AS dense_rank_num
FROM ExamScores
ORDER BY score DESC, student_name ASC;
solutionSQL:
SELECT 
    student_name,
    score,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC, student_name ASC) AS row_num,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS rank_num,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY score DESC) AS dense_rank_num
FROM ExamScores
ORDER BY score DESC, student_name ASC;
